To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the crowding-out of private charitable giving depends upon (i) the extent of competition in the warm-glow motives for giving and (ii) the extent of income effects in the public good motive for giving.
the crowding-out effects of government-financed charitable contributions are exacerbated by competitive warm-glow motives for giving.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the crowding-out of charitable giving by tax-financed contributions of the government.
the effects of tax-financed government contributions to charities on private charitable giving.
the crowding-out effects of tax-financed charitable contributions by the government.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the crowding-out effects of tax-financed government contributions are likely to be substantial.
the crowding-out effects of government contributions depend upon the extent to which the warm-glow motivation for giving is competitive in nature.
the crowding-out effects are not likely to be large, and that the effects of tax-financed contributions are likely to be positive.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
crowding-out effects are not as large as previously thought, and that the competitive nature of warm-glow motives may actually increase the crowding-out effects.
the warm-glow effect of giving is not only an altruistic effect, but it is a competitive effect as well.

the competitive element in the warm-glow motives for giving can exacerbate or attenuated the crowding-out effects of government contributions, and the extent of crowding out is very large when the warm-glow motivation becomes purely competitive.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the crowding out effects of government contributions are more severe than previously thought.
the crowding-out of private contributions may be quite large, even when the government's contribution is relatively small, if individuals are motivated to give primarily by the warm glow of giving.
the competitive nature of the warm-glove motive is a key determinant of the degree to which crowding out occurs.
